question.text: Theodora may have influenced her husband to include women's rights in this legal code that is contained within the Corpus Juris Civilis . This legal code was created to specify the laws of the Byzantine Empire under its namesake emperor.
question.clue: This work contains strikingly accurate transcription of quotes by Gaius and includes several writings by Ulpian as part of the Pandects, or Digest.

swap.text: The Byzantine capital was this city, which was renamed Istanbul after it fell to the Ottomans.
swap.clue: A road called the mese (MEH-say) ran through this city, which may have lost forty percent of its population in a plague in 542 CE. A gigantic cannon designed by Orban sufficed to break through this city's 60-foot-tall Theodosian Walls.

question.text: This Byzantine Emperor tasked Belisarius with reconquering the Mediterranean, and this husband of Theodora was targeted in the Nika Riots.
question.clue: He expelled pagan teachers from the Academy in Athens.

swap.text: Constantinople was earlier sacked during this campaign, which led to the decline of the Byzantine Empire. Enrico Dandolo, the Doge of Venice, had earlier led this campaign.
swap.clue: Pope Innocent III excommunicated all of its participants when they attacked the Dalmatian capital in exchange for assistance from Enrico Dandolo, the doge of Venice.

question.leadin: The 1274 Second Council of Lyon was an unsuccessful attempt to resolve this event.
question.text: Name this 1054 event which permanently divided the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.
question.clue: In the 1960s Athenagoras I and Pope Paul VI mutually lifted excommunication on each other first levied during this historical event.

swap.leadin: Name some things about the times when the use of religious images were opposed by both religious and Byzantine authority.
swap.text: Name that time period during which depictions of religious figures was directly opposed by the leaders of the Eastern Church.
swap.clue: The first attempt to apply this doctrine officially was met with resistance at the Chalke Gate, and it was condemned by the Second Council of Nicaea convoked by Irene.

question.leadin: Description acceptable. Isidore of Kiev apocryphally survived this event by dressing up a dead body with his clothes so that it would be beheaded instead of him.
question.text: Name this event for which the engineer Orban designed a cannon known as "The Basilic" to destroy the Theodosian Walls.
question.answerHtml: Fall of Constantinople [accept answers generally describing a Siege of Constantinople; accept BUT DO NOT REVEAL answers indicating that Constantinople being is captured by the Ottomans; accept the end of the Byzantine Empire]
question.clue: The military leader Giovanni Giustiniani was fatally wounded during this event, which took 40 days to accomplish and was achieved by use of a gate in the northwestern wall, the Kerkoporta.

swap.leadin: Before invading England, Harald Hardrada of Norway served as a mercenary in this military order.
swap.text: Name this elite army unit that served as the personal bodyguards to the emperors of the Byzantine Empire.
swap.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the wonderful world of wartime weaponry.
question.text: This Byzantine ruler was described as inventing several types of trebuchets during the 1097 Siege of Nicaea. This ruler's request of aid from Europe triggered the First Crusade, and his daughter Anna wrote a notable biography of him.
question.clue: Although one rival was forced to give up his territorial gains to assist Henry IV, that rival, Robert Guiscard, defeated this man's forces at the Battle of Dyrrachium.

swap.text: Convened by Marcian, it overturned the decision of the "synod of robbers" at Ephesus two years earlier with regard to the teachings of Eutyches. For 15 points, identify this 451 CE ecumenical council, which approved Pope Leo I's Tome, thus rejecting the Monophysite heresy.
swap.clue: Pope Leo I rejected Canon Twenty-Eight since it ran contradictory to previous canons from Nicaea.

question.text: Eastern European Vikings were given this name by the Byzantines. Six thousand people known by this name formed the Byzantine emperor's personal guard.
question.clue: One theory of Russian religious history points to these people as the means by which the self-sacrificing priest-king entered the Russian pagan pantheon shortly before the spread of Christianity, a transplant from the Norse Odin.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the 1453 conquest of Constantinople by the Ottoman Empire.
swap.text: This church built during the reign of Justinian I, which was once the center of Eastern Orthodox Christianity, was converted into a mosque after the conquest.
swap.clue: On its southwestern entrance of this building is a mosaic of two important emperors presenting models of this building and its city to the Virgin Mary.

question.text: The most famous member of this family temporarily ended the Great Schism with the Second Council of Lyon after reclaiming Constantinople from the Latin Empire. That man, Michael VIII, established this family as the final Byzantine dynasty.
question.clue: Michael VIII founded this dynasty, which expelled the Crusaders from Constantinople in 1261 and were the last to rule Byzantium before the Turkish conquest in 1453.

swap.leadin: This event was preceded by the escape of one prisoner each from the Blue and Green factions, who took shelter in a sanctuary as the public clamored for their release.
swap.text: Name this event which occurred in January 532, in which protesters set fire to the Constantinople Hippodrome but were cornered and defeated by Belisarius and Mundus.

question.text: After the Battle of Adrianople, the Bulgar tsar Kaloyan made a cup from the skull of the first Latin Emperor, who had this name. The final ruler of the Latin Empire, who sold the Crown of Thorns to Louis IX, also had this name.
question.answerHtml: Baldwin [or Baudouin; or Baldwin I; or Baldwin II; or Baldwin of Courtenay]
question.clue: This cousin of Rudyard Kipling highlighted the power of aerial attacks by noting that "the bomber will always get through."

swap.leadin: Name some people whose writings serve as important primary sources about the Byzantine Empire.
swap.text: This woman may have been inspired by the material laid out by her husband Nikephoros Bryennios the Younger to write a chronicle of her father's rule named the Alexiad.
swap.clue: This twelfth-century Byzantine princess became one of the first known women historians by penning the Alexiad, which narrates the dynasty-establishing reign of her father Alexios I.

question.leadin: The Arvanites under Peter Bua rose up in revolt in this principality in the 15th century.
question.text: Name this principality in the Peloponnese that was first ruled over by Manuel Kantakouzenos in 1349. Along with Epirus, the despot of this region was usually a son of the Byzantine Emperor.

swap.text: The second ruler of this dynasty, Leo VI the Wise, prescribed harsh punishments for counterfeiting alchemists in his Book of the Eparch. Leo completed the Basilika law code named after the founder of this dynasty, Basil I.
swap.clue: Chief military figures from this period include Nicephorus Phocas and an Armenian usurper, John Tzimisces, though its most notable battlefield accomplishment may have come against the army of Tsar Samuel.

question.leadin: This ruler, who introduced jousting and other Western European traditions to his kingdom, was hailed as a chivalric model by contemporaries, such as his chronicler John Kinnamos.
question.text: Identify this grandson of Alexius I, a Byzantine emperor who attempted an alliance with the papacy under Adrian IV. His attempt to regain Anatolia was halted at the Battle of Myriokephalon.
question.clue: While this ruler's armies besieged the island of Corfu, the Venetians mocked this ruler by having an African slave impersonate him.

swap.text: A Pecheneg siege of Constantinople in 1090 was defeated by this Byzantine emperor and his Cuman allies. His daughter Anna Comnenus wrote a biography of him, and he ruled during the First Crusade.
swap.clue: This ruler lost the Battle of Dyrrhachium to Robert Guiscard during a Norman invasion of his territory; Guiscard's death is related in Book 6 of a historical text compiled by this man's daughter, Anna, and named for him.
